fatty acyl CoA is transferred to carnitine to form a fatty acyl-carnitine by the action of palmitoyl carnitine transferase 1 (CPT 1)
(Fig. 5). This occurs on the outer mitochondrial membrane and the fatty acyl-carnitine is transported into the mitochondrial matrix
in exchange for free carnitine. Once within the matrix the fatty acyl group is transferred back to CoASH to yield the fatty acyl-CoA
that can enter the pathway of b oxidation. CPT1 is strongly inhibited by malonyl CoA which is abundant in the cell at times of high
rates of glucose metabolism and therefore inhibits fatty acid oxidation. The b oxidation of fatty acids (Fig. 4) involves a dehydro-
genase producing FADH2, followed by a hydratase (addition of water), a further dehydrogenase producing NADH and ﬁnally a thi-
